name: TVS Motor Company Ltd
title: TVS Motor Company Ltd - 532343 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: TVS Motor FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 47,270 crores with record Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores and 13.1% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: TVS Motor reported record FY26 volume of 5.9 million units (up 24%), revenue of INR 47,270 crores (up 30%) and operating PBT of INR 4,975 crores (up 40%). Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores grew 36% YoY with EBITDA margin of 13.1%, against 6.5% when the margin recovery began. Management flagged near-term supply disruptions (gas, labour at Tier 2 suppliers, raw material timing, container lead times) and 3-5% commodity cost inflation, and guided to a strong single-digit industry growth in FY27 with capex of about INR 3,500 crores.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 37% from INR 4,450 crores; margin up 60 bps from 12.3%
vs INR 1,172 crores in Q4 FY25
vs INR 851 crores in Q4 FY25
PBT up 22%; book up 15% from INR 26,647 crores

segments.name: 2-wheeler ICE (domestic)
segments.commentary: FY26 2W ICE sales grew 22% vs industry 12%; Q4 domestic ICE grew 26% vs industry 24%. Scooter category share is about 38% (including EV), which management expects to exceed 40%.

segments.name: Electric 2-wheeler
segments.commentary: FY26 EV 2W sales of 3.7 lakh units, up 33% from 2.8 lakh; Q4 EV sales 115,000, up 51%. EV penetration rose to 6.6% for FY26 (6.2% prior) and 7.8% in Q4 (7.1% prior). FY26 EV revenue about INR 5,000 crores.

segments.name: 3-wheeler
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 220,000 units, up 63% from 135,000; Q4 60,000 units, up 65% from 37,000.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record FY26 international sales of 15.8 lakh units, up 33%; Q4 international revenue INR 2,999 crores. Q4 international sales grew 23%. Spare parts revenue in Q4 about INR 1,122 crores.

segments.name: TVS Credit
segments.commentary: FY26 PBT INR 1,248 crores (up 22%); Q4 PBT INR 348 crores (up 15%). Added about 53 lakh new customers, total base about 2.4 crore; rated AA+.

segments.name: Norton (overseas subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Majority of the roughly INR 2,400 crores FY26 investment went to Norton; new models Manx, Manx R, Atlas and Atlas GT to be launched with Q2 FY27 as a key milestone. Some models to be built at Solihull and others at Hosur.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic industry growth guided at a strong single digit; TVS aims to grow ahead of the industry in both domestic and international markets.
Q1 FY27 expected to show very good growth ahead of the industry in both retail and dispatches, as supply constraints ease in May and are expected to clear by end-May or early June.
FY27 capex expected at about INR 3,500 crores: about INR 2,000 crores on product development, over INR 1,000 crores on 1.5 million unit capacity addition, and higher R&D spend.
Overseas investment in FY27 expected to be about 70% of FY26 level (INR 500-600 crores lower than INR 2,400 crores), though not zero.

Management declined to give margin guidance; said cost inflation of 3-5% of revenue is significant, with about 35% offset so far through price increases, and cited mix, scale and cost reduction as offsets.
Management expects 2W EV and scooter segments to grow well in FY27; the economy segment is expected to face challenges.
capex_capacity: Immediate plan to add about 1.5 million units of capacity, taking total to about 8.3 million units; work started in Q4 FY26 and the first significant addition in 12 months.
Capacity planning for FY28-29 under review quarter by quarter; aim is for capacity not to constrain growth.
EV production currently averages around 40,000 units/month (FY26 average 30,000-32,000), with a target of 50,000 per month soon.
Norton products in development at Hosur and Solihull; new Norton models expected in Q2 FY27.
Overseas: Dubai strategic investment about INR 300 crores made; TVS Credit investment about INR 200 crores in FY26.
demand_pricing: Demand described as strong across domestic and international for all models, but supply was the binding constraint. Dealer inventory is kept at 21-30 days and is being rebuilt; channel stock is expected to normalise by end-May or early June.
Commodity cost inflation (steel, aluminium, crude derivatives, gas) estimated at 3-5% of revenue; about 35% offset through price increases so far.
PLI incentive income for Q4 was about 0.9% of revenue.
Ronin monthly domestic volume crossed 8,000 units; management targets above 10,000. Indonesia averaged about 20,000 units per month, up from 17,000.
Africa and Asia are core; LatAm is a multi-year focus. International container lead times rose about 15% (around 8-10 days) amid geopolitical disruption.
3-wheeler: VAHAN share of EV 3W rising; new launches include King Kargo EV and King Kargo Heavy Duty CNG cargo; Hyundai JDA signed to co-develop an EV 3W.

qa_highlights.question: What growth is expected in FY27 for domestic and international, and how will segments perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong single-digit industry growth, with scooters, EVs and premium/super-premium growing well and the economy segment facing headwinds. TVS expects to outgrow the industry.

qa_highlights.question: What commodity inflation and price increases are expected in Q1 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation is about 3-5% of revenue, with about 35% offset by price increases so far. Mix, scale and cost reduction are the other levers.

qa_highlights.question: What are current 2W and 3W production capacities and the planned additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is being increased by 1.5 million units to about 8.3 million. Management said this is the first significant addition in 12 months, and capacity will not constrain growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where are supply-chain constraints (raw materials, labour, rare earths) and channel stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Constraints are energy/gas, Tier 2 labour shortages and raw material timing. May is better than April, and channel stock should normalise by end-May or early June. Q4 international revenue was INR 2,999 crores and spare parts INR 1,122 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management cautious for the next two quarters, and what are the risks to demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is strong and the uncertainty is on raw material timing and Tier 2 disruption, which it expects to clear within 2-3 weeks. Geopolitical risk is monitored industry-wide.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 investment plan and what is the Norton spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas investment is about INR 2,400 crores in FY26 (mainly Norton) and is expected to be about 70% of that in FY27. Total FY27 capex is about INR 3,500 crores, of which about INR 2,000 crores is product development.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV capacity and international EV plan?
qa_highlights.answer: EV output is about 40,000 units per month, moving toward 50,000. Asian markets are taking a growing share of EV volumes, with iQube and Orbiter launched there.

qa_highlights.question: Will Norton products be made in India, and what is the Hyundai EV 3W partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: One high-end Norton model will be built at Solihull and the others in India, using the Hosur plant. The Hyundai JDA is for co-developing an EV 3W, with Hyundai leading design; management gave no revenue or timeline details.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation of 3-5% of revenue with only about 35% offset so far; margin sustainability beyond Q1 FY27 is uncertain.
Supply-chain disruption from gas prices, Tier 2 labour shortages and raw material timing; management expects normalisation in 2-3 weeks.
International container lead times up about 15%, with West Asia conflict and logistics delays affecting distributor planning.
Economy segment demand pressure from inflation and fuel prices; El Nino risk to rainfall and rural demand in Q3-Q4.
Norton and other overseas investments (about INR 2,400 crores in FY26) must yield revenue; Norton launches expected in Q2 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the long-term trajectory, but cautious near term: management repeatedly flagged supply-chain constraints and commodity inflation for the next one to two quarters. Answers on margins and the Hyundai partnership were deliberately high-level, with detail deferred to launch.
key_quotes: We are expecting a good single-digit growth on the industry this year.
Immediately, we are looking at increasing the capacity by another 1.5 million, to go to somewhere around 8.3 million because the demand is good
Next year, the investments will be much lower.
We will make sure that we will not -- we will continue to invest in technology, R&D, innovation and brand building.

adds.what: 1.5 million units capacity addition, taking total to about 8.3 million units

growth.why: Management guides to a strong single-digit industry growth in FY27 and aims to outgrow the industry, backed by work started on a 1.5 million unit capacity addition (about 8.3 million total, over INR 1,000 crores capex) and new Norton models in Q2 FY27, though the capacity timing is not stated and margin guidance was withheld.
